correctness.rationale: Literal deletion-ball collision characterization was rederived. Any nonadjacent parent consumes one or two distinct weight-one marker outputs; loops separated by two share a weight-two output; this gives the independent-two-path loop cap and exact \(f(m)\). Adjacent-ones parents share the all-zero output, so at most one can occur; the boundary case sharpens to \(1+f(m-1)\). An explicit four-periodic marker matching attains it, and the necessary-and-sufficient collision criteria establish no hidden weight-two collision. All bounds and the \(n=2\) exception were checked. The standalone checker confirms 79,002 pairwise collision decisions and 249 constructions, with exact maximum independent sets through length 10; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual research-record queries, existing accessible findings, and primary literature were compared by their error balls and logical implications, not merely titles. The closest 2022/2016 burst-code papers treat general codes/at-most bursts, while 2012 weight-partition methods address arbitrary deletions, none inspected proving this exact all-length fixed-weight result. Some equivalent earlier specialization may be unlocated; source inspection scopes and limitations are recorded.
residual_risks: A classical or differently named treatment of very sparse burst-deletion codes might contain an implicit equivalent.
Publicly indexed research-record search summaries cannot establish nonexistence of an unindexed, privately held, or inaccessible result.

value.rationale: The capacity is a natural exact zero-error invariant for fixed-composition synchronization coding, has a sharp infinite-family formula, a direct no-search construction and a matching-with-loops reduction exposing the four-periodic structure. This is not a mere restriction of an unrestricted-deletion optimum and gives concrete optimal sparse-marker codebooks for every length.
